verdict.rationale: GitHub's docs say anyone can fork a repository to create a new repository on GitHub, and they describe GitHub's pull request workflow for creating and reviewing code, including reviewing and collaborating on PRs from mobile. Together these deliver the core of the story, but the evidence never explicitly shows a PR opened from a fork back to the upstream repository. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of cross-fork pull requests to the upstream repo, maintainer controls over outside-contributor PRs (e.g., allowing edits from maintainers or approving workflow runs for forks), and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an open-source-maintainer, I can let outside contributors fork my repository and propose changes back via pull requests
